newsitem.title: USA: McKesson says acquisition boost to earnings.
newsitem.headline: McKesson says acquisition boost to earnings.

text.p: McKesson Corp said on Friday that it's agreement to buy the drug unit of FoxMeyer Health Corp would boost earnings within 90 to 180 days after the deal is closed. The deal is expected to close in mid-November.
McKesson has agreed to buy FoxMeyer Drug Co and its affiliates for $80 million in cash.
The deal allows for the purchase to occur through an expedited auction process. It is to be submitted today to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware.
FoxMeyer has been operating as a debtor in possession under the protection of Chapter 11.

"The acquisition of FoxMeyer clearly furthers our business strategy," McKesson President and Chief Operating Officer Mark Pulido said in a statement. "McKesson has made significant investments in strategic initiatives to advance the success of our customers. With this acquisition, these investments can be leveraged by quickly rolling out our programs to FoxMeyer's broad base of retail and institutional customers."

Pulido said the acquisition also will allow McKesson to "make significant improvements" to its cost structure. He added that he believed it would allow the company to reduce its annual fixed costs by more than $80 million.
McKesson provides pharmaceuticals and health-care products and services. FoxMeyer distributes pharmaceuticals, health and beauty aids and other products.
